decisions.reason: Uses ls-remote-tags.txt (listing jumps v0.9.1 to v0.9.7, v0.9.5 absent) and sync-script.sh (only git push HEAD:main per mirror, no tag refspec) to explain attempt 1 as a tag-distribution gap tied to ref resolution failure, explicitly ruling out consumer network, command, or missing npm package.

Combines dsh-version.txt (0.1.1-rc.2) with compat-table.md (v0.9.7 targets 0.1.2-alpha.1 with the useConversation seat) to explain that a newer-API artifact on an older runtime lacks the expected seat at registration time, and states that install success and restarting cannot fix a deterministic artifact-vs-host API mismatch.

The report honors the freeze, notices v0.9.3 is also absent from the mirror, cites its rc.1 verification plus the additive rc.2 note, and treats #v0.9.3 as the preferable pin after maintainer back-fill without inventing a SHA or requiring a DSH upgrade. However, its concrete immediate command pins #v0.9.1, whose rc-cohort compatibility is not verified by any fixture evidence (compat-table covers only v0.9.3 and v0.9.7), and the explicit #v0.9.3-after-publication install command is only implied, diluting the required v0.9.3-centered remedy.

Proposes pushing tags to every mirror (git push <remote> --tags or an explicit refs/tags/* refspec) alongside the branch sync, grounded in the branch-only script, and adds verification that documented/pinned tags resolve on each mirror via ls-remote comparison gates in CI.

Routes README install commands by consumer DSH version: an explicit compatibility table with 'last release supporting DSH 0.1.1-rc.x: v0.9.3' callouts for rc users and newest-tag-requires-alpha.1+ notes for alpha users, plus install-time cohort enforcement; avoids a single newest-tag default, restart advice, and untested-future-alpha generalization.
